Func - Get declared arguments.vi

Owning Palette: FuncVI Development

The VI returns values and data types of arbitrary function arguments according to the given specification. The VI makes it possible to define default values for optional function arguments if they are omitted in a function call. The VI allows obtaining a variable name as an argument value.

Details

Click the parameters for more information

 

InstanceRef is the reference to the CalcExpress instance that evaluates a CalcExpress expression.
arg list array specifies a list of function arguments. Wire this terminal to respective control on a block diagram of a FuncVI in order to provide the VI with access to all arguments passed to a FuncVI. Click here for more information.
type contains a code of the argument data type. Refer to the Data Types topic for details.
str contains either a string value of an argument or a name of variable if type is equal to 2 (Identifier). str is empty string if type equals 1 (DBL Number). If an argument has either one of Complex data types or a user-defined data type, str contains a value in the Flattened-To-String format.
num contains numeric value of an argument if it has DBL Number data type.
min arg num. Typically, if arg list contains all function arguments, it specifies a minimum number of arguments that can be operated by a function. If the size of arg list is less than a value of this control, the VI produces an error. By default, min arg num is equal to 1.
max arg num. Typically, if arg list contains all function arguments, it specifies a maximum number of arguments that can be operated by a function. If the size of arg list is greater than a value of this control, the VI produces an error. By default, max arg num is equal to 100.
error in specifies an error status before this VI executes. The VI runs normally only if error in is FALSE.
arg descriptors specifies attributes of expected arguments. The VI verifies data types and returns values of the arguments declared in this control, it ignores arguments not declared here.
index of the argument in arg list. It is the same as an argument index in a function call if arg list contains all function arguments.
type specifies an expected data type code of the argument. Any argument data type is allowed if type is equal to -1. The VI produces an error if data type of an actual argument doesn't match the expected data type and type is not -1.
The VI returns variable values unless type is set to Identifier. If type is Identifier, the VI does not attempt to get a variable value and returns the identifier (a variable name).
default num specifies a default value for arguments of DBL Number data type. It is returned as a value of the respective argument if index is beyond of arg list boundaries.
default str specifies a default value for arguments of data types other than DBL Number. It is returned as a value of the respective argument if index is beyond of arg list boundaries.
num list. The VI returns numeric values through this indicator. The size of num list is the same as the size of arg descriptors. Order of elements corresponds to the order of descriptors in arg descriptors. An element value is valid if the respective element of type list indicates the value has DBL Number data type.
str list. The VI returns string values through this indicator. The size of str list is the same as the size of arg descriptors. Order of elements corresponds to the order of descriptors in arg descriptors. An element value is valid if the respective element of type list indicates the value has data type other than DBL Number.  If an argument has either one of Complex data types or a user-defined data type, its value is present in the Flattened-To-String format.
type list. The VI returns value data types through this indicator. Elements of type list contain actual data types of the respective elements in num list and str list. Note that a value data type is the same as type specified in the respective element of arg descriptors unless the descriptor contains -1 in its type member. The size of type list is the same as the size of arg descriptors. Order of elements corresponds to the order of descriptors in arg descriptors.
error out returns TRUE if either error in is TRUE or the VI detects an error condition. If an error detected, the VI puts an error description to the Error Protocol.

 

Func - Get declared arguments.vi - details

The VI is intended for use in FuncVIs.
The VI verifies both number of arguments and argument data types according to the specifications. If the VI detects any error, it returns an error status and posts the error description to the Error Protocol. A CalcExpress VI returns the error description when it completes evaluating the expression.

For details, see the FuncVI Development topic. Also see Example of use.
